pr_body:
### What does it do?

Accepts components also when transferring the links. This fixes the errors related to missing relations inside components after a data transfer (export and import or transfer)

### Why is it needed?

To allow relations inside of components to be transferred

### How to test it?

Create a content type with a component that has a relation to another content type inside it and add some data to that content type. Try to transfer or export and import to another Strapi project that has the same content type and everything should be transferred, as shown in [this Loom video](https://www.loom.com/share/27a1d2627261478088f91764cc34f771?sid=33193cbe-78d0-4e1f-9180-f1c330c7b5e5)

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)

issue_context.title: Collection type relationships missing after CLi Transfer
issue_context.body: ## Bug report ### Required System information - Node.js version: **v16.20.0** - NPM version: **8.19.3** - Strapi version: **v4.10.5** - Database: **SQL** - Operating system: **macOS=>ASW** & **macOS=>macOS** - Is your project Javascript or Typescript: **Typescript** ### Describe the bug #### Background We have content/components that are repeated in multiple page. To stop us from adding this content to each page we have a Collection type that stores that content, that is turn is referenced to a component, which is then added to a dynamic zone within a page. This allows us to add multiple new pages, and then add "ConentBlock1" to the dynamic zone of each page. #### Bug When transferring data via the CLi all relationships with Collection Types are lost. #### Local instance #### Destination instance after transfer ### Steps to reproduce the behaviour 1. Create a Collection type 2. Create a component that has relationship with the above Collection 3. Create a `Page` collection Type 4. Add a `Dynamic Zone` to `Page` 5. Add the component created above to the available components in the `Dynamic Zone` 6. In Content Manager add some data the Collection Type you created, save & publish 7. Add a new page 8. Add content to dynamic zone of page 9. Select the Component above 10. Publish page 11. Ensure content is as expected 12. Perform transfer of data from local instance to remote instance 13. Observe, although the Component in the dynamic Zone is present in the page structure, the link to the instance of that collection type is not. ### Expected behaviour Collection Relationships remain intact ### Screenshots #### Successful transfer
